If the graph of $y=f(x)$ is shown above, then

${\int }_{-2}^{5}f(x)\,\text{d}x=$
{{field-1}}.
feedback.worked_solution:
The graph consists of $2$ parts: the arc of the quarter circle for $x\in [-2,1)$ and the line segment for $x\in [1,5].$ So, we can use the additive property of integrals to get

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{-2}^{5}f(x)\,\text{d}x={{{\int }_{-2}^{1}f(x)\,\text{d}x}_{⏟}}_{{A}_{1}}+{{{\int }_{1}^{5}f(x)\,\text{d}x}_{⏟}}_{{A}_{2}}.\end{aligned}
$$

- The $1$st integral represents the signed area between the curve and the $x$-axis, where $x\in [-2,1).$ The corresponding region is a quarter circle of radius $3,$ so we find the area using the formula

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}_{1} & =\frac{1}{4}\pi {r}^{2} \\  & =\frac{1}{4}\pi \cdot (3)^{2} \\  & =\frac{9\pi }{4}.\end{aligned}
$$

- The $2$nd integral represents the signed area between the curve and the $x$-axis, where $x\in [1,5].$ The corresponding region is a right triangle, so we find the area using the formula

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}_{2} & =\frac{1}{2}bh \\  & =\frac{1}{2}2\cdot 4 \\  & =4.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{-2}^{5}f(x)\,\text{d}x & ={A}_{1}+{A}_{2} \\  & =\frac{9\pi }{4}+4 \\  & =\frac{9\pi +16}{4}.\end{aligned}
$$
